highlights.title: Your answer shows once, on the question
highlights.text: When you answer a bot's question, the card itself says "You picked …" or "You answered: …", instead of repeating your answer in a bubble below it.

highlights.title: Named buttons in the phone chat header
highlights.text: On a phone, the chat header's buttons now have captions: Team, Pin, Edit and Browser. The row of chips fades on the side that has more to scroll.

highlights.title: Approval options in plain words
highlights.text: Each approval option now says plainly what a bot does on its own and when a card asks you first, without jargon.

highlights.title: A reply's name stays put when it lands
highlights.text: The name above a reply that's still being written already looks the way it will when the reply is done, so nothing changes size when it finishes.

highlights.title: The island never shows what a bot searches for
highlights.text: The desktop island says "Searching files", "Searching the web" or "Starting a helper". The words a bot searches for stay in the chat.

highlights.title: Follow-ups never read a customer's words as yours
highlights.text: When a bot follows up in a chat a customer or a connected agent also wrote in, their lines are marked as theirs, never as yours.

fixes: After a failed step, "Let me know what else you need" no longer shows Blocked; "Let me know which file to use" still does.
Read tools like get_release or list_merge_requests get Allow once again on Telegram and the island; commands and pushes still don't.
A refused tool call that a bot retries now leaves one "refused" entry, not one per retry.
A hand-off passes on your own message as the request; a customer's, agent's or bot's words go along marked as theirs.
The island's Allow once works for plain reads of mail, files, posts and payments; sending, paying and deleting still need the card.
The perch shows on a Mac again (it stayed hidden since 0.9.15), and ⌥⌘K gives it the keyboard.
